correctness.rationale: The exact S^3 orthogonality normalization gives b_n=4(n+1)^2/π Re[β_{(-1)^n}/((z²+n²)(z²+(n+2)²))]. The positive denominator modulus reduces sign to P_ε((n+1)²). Every quadratic on either parity sequence of squares is decided by its leading coefficient and at most two vertex-bracketing squares. β_ε≠0 and Im(conjugate(z)²)=2aω guarantee an eventually positive coefficient in each parity in every accepted regime, proving strict definiteness. At integer ω=m the amplitude factor is strictly positive, and the sign polynomial a[(X+r−1)²+4r(1−m²)] strictly increases on X≥1, with value ar(a²+4−3m²) at X=1. The negative-mode cutoff follows from its unique crossing. Symbolic expansion was recomputed; a standalone checker passed 40 direct-integral checks, 500 parameter finite-sign comparisons, and 20 threshold-side tests. No finite experiment is used to infer the infinite-degree result.

value.rationale: An exact global validity criterion for oscillatory geodesic covariance functions on S³ is motivated by the need to know when negative correlations produce positive semidefinite interpolation matrices. A continuous two-parameter family has infinitely many harmonic constraints; the theorem compresses them to bounded finite arithmetic with exact equality handling. The integer-frequency subfamily has a curvature-shifted sharp threshold and a complete contiguous negative-harmonic classification, a substantive spectral boundary distinct from the Euclidean or circle model. This resolves a natural family rather than a routine isolated number.
